topic.title: Concept Learning and Explicit Explanatory Structure
topic.overview: This cluster connects learning concepts with constructing structured explanations of observations. The recent abstracts describe generative models of student cognitive structure and executable latent programs that explain how observed phenomena arise. The common ambition is a reusable representation of relationships, rather than a predictor tied only to one output label.
topic.whyItMatters: Explicit structure can support interpretation and transfer when new tasks require recombining what was learned. However, a useful predictive representation is not automatically a faithful account of how a person thinks or how the world works.
topic.evolution: Archival titles from the 1980s and 1990s concern concept induction, prior knowledge, analogy, and causality, but their missing abstracts limit detailed historical claims. The available 2026 evidence emphasizes modular cognitive representations and learned executable theories. This supports a thematic connection, not a verified chain of intellectual influence.
openQuestions: How can explanatory programs be tested against alternative theories with similar predictions?
What evidence validates a learned cognitive structure beyond downstream accuracy?
